newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian First Bank spends on IT.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian First Bank spends on IT.

text.p: First Bank of Nigeria Plc, the country's oldest bank, said on Tuesday that it would invest most of the proceeds from a forthcoming public share offer in information technology.
The bank is to offer for public subscription 200 million shares at 10.50 naira between September 1 and September 26, 1997.

At a meeting with the parties to the offer in Lagos, First Bank's chief executive officer, Joseph Sanusi listed areas where the proceeds -- more than two billion naira ($24.5 million) -- would be spent to maintain its position in the industry.
Of the sum, one billion or 55 percent would be invested in computers, electronics and telecommunications, Sanusi said. He said the establishment of new branches would account for 45 percent.
The cost of the public offer is put at 97.9 million naira, five percent of the total expected proceeds.

A bank spokesman said the proceeds "would also enable the bank to introduce state of the art technology in banking service and facilitate the establishment of strategic branches in key locations to complement existing ones."
Its market capitalisation is put at about 10.8 billion naira.
